subject: bull shark
title: Bull Sharks Pick Their Friends, and Scientists Watched for Six Years

scenes.text: Bull sharks don't just gather. They choose their friends.
In Fiji, scientists followed 184 bull sharks for six years.
They logged which sharks swam within one body length of each other, and who followed whom.
It wasn't random. The sharks kept choosing certain companions and swimming side by side.
And they mostly picked partners close to their own size.
Not a lone killer after all. Even a bull shark has a favourite swimming buddy.

description:
Bull sharks form social preferences and choose who they swim with.
A six-year study of 184 bull sharks at Fiji's Shark Reef Marine Reserve, published in Animal Behaviour, found they favour certain companions, especially sharks of similar size.
Did you think sharks had friends?
first_comment: The researchers sorted the sharks into three age groups, including old, post-reproductive adults. Which ocean animal would you least expect to have friends?
